guarded_patterns.explanation: git credential fill queries the configured credential helper and prints the resolved username AND PASSWORD in plaintext to stdout. Run bare -- even 'just to check it works' or to debug a hang -- the credential value lands directly in the agent transcript, shell history, and any process capturing the terminal, and cannot be un-printed. This happened for real on 2026-08-27: a live Forgejo PAT was printed in full to an agent transcript while debugging a curl auth header, requiring rotation.

redirect.reason_template: git credential fill prints 'password=<value>' to stdout -- never invoke it bare, even for a quick debug check. Capture the whole invocation into a shell variable and only ever reference the variable, never its expansion: TOKEN=$(git credential fill <<< $'protocol=https\nhost=<host>\n' | sed -n 's/^password=//p'); then use "$TOKEN" (e.g. in a curl -H header) without ever printing it.

guarded_patterns.explanation: Force-push flags can rewrite git history and lose commits

redirect.reason_template: Removed --force/-f/--force-with-lease from git push; force-pushing can rewrite remote history and lose commits. Retrying as a normal push preserves the requested commits without rewriting the remote.

guarded_patterns.explanation: A git commit without an explicit pathspec commits the entire staged index, which may include unrelated pre-staged changes

redirect.reason_template: git commit without a pathspec can sweep unrelated staged changes into the commit. Pass the same file paths to git commit that you passed to git add -- git commit <paths> -m "...".

guarded_patterns.explanation: Pushing when remote HEAD has moved forward risks rejection and creates merge conflicts

redirect.reason_template: Remote HEAD has moved forward since your last fetch/pull. Run 'git pull' first to integrate remote changes before pushing.
